places.title: Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya)
places.architect: Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus
places.why: Justinian’s church, whose 31-metre dome seems to float on a ring of 40 windows, was the largest cathedral in the world for nearly a thousand years and the model for the Ottoman mosques around it. Its gold mosaics survive in the upper galleries, next to the minarets, calligraphic roundels and mihrab added after 1453.

places.title: Sultan Ahmed Mosque (Blue Mosque)
places.why: Facing Hagia Sophia across a garden square, the last great imperial mosque of the classical age rises in a cascade of domes and half-domes framed by six minarets. More than 20,000 İznik tiles in blues and greens line its prayer hall, which is lit by some 200 windows.

photos.file: Exterior of Sultan Ahmed I Mosque in Istanbul, Turkey 002.jpg
photos.author: Moonik

places.title: Topkapı Palace
places.architect: Builders of Mehmed II, later additions by Mimar Sinan and others
places.why: The residence of the sultans for four centuries spreads over the tip of the historic peninsula as a sequence of courtyards, kiosks and pavilions rather than one building. The tiled rooms of the Harem and the marble terraces over the Bosphorus and the Golden Horn are its highlights.

photos.file: Palacio de Topkapı, Estambul, Turquía, 2024-09-30, DD 67.jpg
photos.author: Diego Delso

photos.file: Dome of Baghdad Kiosk, Topkapı Palace (1).jpg
photos.author: Till Niermann

places.title: Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı)
places.why: A sixth-century underground reservoir built under Justinian, its brick vaults carried by 336 columns, many of them taken from older buildings. Walkways lead over the shallow water to two column bases carved with Medusa heads.

photos.file: Cisterna Basílica, Estambul, Turquía, 2024-09-28, DD 58-60 HDR.jpg
photos.author: Diego Delso

photos.file: A medusa head at the basilica cistern.jpg
photos.author: Tcyagizefem

places.title: Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı)
places.why: One of the largest and oldest covered markets in the world, a town of vaulted streets, hans and some 4,000 shops grown around Mehmed II’s two domed bedestens. Its gates open onto the old caravanserais and workshops of the surrounding market district.

photos.file: 21 Gran Basar d'Istanbul (Kapalıçarşı), botiga de llums.jpg
photos.author: Enric

places.title: Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı)
places.why: The L-shaped vaulted market of the New Mosque complex, built in the 1660s and long paid for by duties on goods from Egypt, still sells spices, dried fruit and sweets. Around it the streets of Tahtakale are the busiest market quarter of the old city.

photos.file: 18 Basar Egipci d'Istanbul (Mısır Çarşısı), parada d'espècies.jpg
photos.author: Enric

places.title: Süleymaniye Mosque
places.why: Sinan’s grandest mosque crowns the third hill above the Golden Horn, its great dome set over a vast, evenly lit prayer hall. The complex keeps its madrasas, hospital, kitchen, baths and the tombs of Süleyman and Hürrem, and its terrace is one of the best views of the city.

photos.file: PXL 20241210 102315450 Suleymaniye Mosque Süleymaniye Camii Istanbul Turkey 12.jpg
photos.author: Sourabh.biswas003

photos.file: PXL 20241210 102315450 Suleymaniye Mosque Süleymaniye Camii Istanbul Turkey 19.jpg
photos.author: Sourabh.biswas003

photos.file: PXL 20241210 102315450 Suleymaniye Mosque Süleymaniye Camii Istanbul Turkey 05.jpg
photos.author: Sourabh.biswas003

places.title: Galata Tower
places.why: The stone tower the Genoese built at the top of their walled colony has watched over the Golden Horn since 1348. Its gallery gives a full circle of views over the historic peninsula, the Bosphorus and the steep lanes of Galata below.

places.title: Dolmabahçe Palace
places.why: The sultans moved from Topkapı to this European-style palace stretched along 600 metres of the Bosphorus shore, a mix of baroque, neoclassical and Ottoman forms. Its ceremonial hall hangs one of the largest crystal chandeliers in the world; the domed Dolmabahçe Mosque by the same architects stands at its southern end.

photos.file: Palacio de Dolmabahçe, Estambul, Turquía, 2024-09-29, DD 24.jpg
photos.author: Diego Delso

places.title: The Bosphorus (İstanbul Boğazı)
places.why: The 30-kilometre strait between Europe and Asia is the city’s main avenue, lined on both shores with wooden yalı mansions, palaces, fortresses and old fishing villages. The public ferries from Eminönü and the shore walk through Arnavutköy and Bebek are the way to see it.

places.title: İstiklal Avenue and Taksim Square
places.why: The old Grande Rue de Péra runs for 1.3 km from Tünel to Taksim, lined with 19th-century apartment blocks, arcades such as the Çiçek Pasajı, churches and consulates, with the historic tram down its middle. At its end Taksim Square is the city’s main public square.

photos.file: Nostalgic tram on Istiklal Avenue in Istanbul.jpg
photos.author: Janderk1968

places.title: Hippodrome (Sultanahmet Square)
places.why: The square keeps the outline of the Byzantine chariot-racing arena, the centre of the city’s public life for a thousand years. Its monuments still stand on the old central barrier: the Egyptian obelisk raised by Theodosius I and the bronze Serpent Column from Delphi, with the İbrahim Pasha Palace on its western side.

photos.file: Blue Mosque from Turk ve Islam Museum in 2016 1443.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

photos.file: Obelisco de Teodosio, Estambul, Turquía, 2024-09-28, DD 129.jpg
photos.author: Diego Delso
Gryffindor This panoramic image was created with Autostitch (stitched images may differ from reality) .

places.title: Chora Church (Kariye)
places.why: A small Byzantine church near the land walls with the finest surviving cycle of late Byzantine mosaics and frescoes, commissioned by the statesman Theodore Metochites in the 1310s. The Anastasis fresco in its side chapel is one of the masterpieces of medieval painting.

places.title: Theodosian Walls and Yedikule Fortress
places.why: The double land walls of Theodosius II run 6.5 km from the Sea of Marmara to the Golden Horn and held Constantinople for a thousand years. Along them stand the Yedikule fortress around the Golden Gate and the Palace of the Porphyrogenitus, and outside them lie market gardens cultivated since Byzantine times.

photos.file: Istanbul Yedikule Entrance and South tower in 2006 3456.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

places.title: Maiden’s Tower (Kız Kulesi)
places.why: A small tower on an islet off Üsküdar, first a Byzantine watch post and rebuilt by the Ottomans as a lighthouse, is the emblem of the Bosphorus. It is best seen from the Salacak shore at sunset, against the skyline of the historic peninsula.

places.title: Princes’ Islands (Büyükada and Heybeliada)
places.why: A ferry ride from the city, the car-free islands of the Sea of Marmara were the summer retreat of Istanbul’s Greek, Armenian and Jewish families. Büyükada and Heybeliada are lined with wooden mansions and pine woods, with Greek monasteries on their hilltops.

places.title: Kadıköy and Moda
places.why: The heart of the Asian side, a ferry ride from Eminönü: the food market streets behind the pier, then the late Ottoman and early republican apartment blocks of Moda. The Moda shore park on the Sea of Marmara is where the city comes to watch the sun set behind the historic peninsula.

places.title: Balat and Fener
places.why: Two old Golden Horn quarters of the city’s Jewish and Greek communities, with steep streets of colourful row houses, synagogues and churches. Above them rises the red-brick Phanar Greek Orthodox College, and the Ecumenical Patriarchate keeps its seat at the Church of St George.

places.title: Ortaköy Mosque (Büyük Mecidiye Camii)
places.why: A small neo-baroque mosque on a pier at the water’s edge, its tall windows and slender minarets framed by the Bosphorus Bridge. The square around it, with its cafés and stalls, is one of the liveliest spots on the European shore.

places.title: Rumeli Hisarı
places.why: Mehmed II built this fortress in a few months in 1452 at the narrowest point of the Bosphorus, to close the strait before the siege of Constantinople. Its three great towers and curtain walls climb the steep hillside above the water.

photos.author: Roger W from Sarasota, Florida, U.S.A.

places.title: Eminönü, the New Mosque and Galata Bridge
places.why: The busiest waterfront of the old city, where the ferries leave for Asia and up the Bosphorus, is dominated by the New Mosque, begun in 1597 and finished in 1665. The Galata Bridge, lined with anglers, crosses the Golden Horn from here to Karaköy.

photos.file: Mezquita Nueva, Estambul, Turquía, 2024-09-29, DD 39-41 HDR.jpg
photos.author: Diego Delso

places.title: Eyüp Sultan Mosque and Pierre Loti Hill
places.why: The holiest Muslim shrine of Istanbul, the tomb of the Prophet’s companion Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, stands in a mosque complex rebuilt in 1800 and surrounded by cemeteries of carved Ottoman tombstones. A path through them, or the cable car, climbs to the café on Pierre Loti Hill above the upper Golden Horn.

places.title: Gülhane Park
places.why: The former outer garden of Topkapı Palace, below its walls, is a public park of plane trees, flowerbeds and fountains running down towards Seraglio Point. It is planted with tulips every spring.

photos.file: Istanbul Tulip Festival in Gülhane Park (01).jpg
photos.author: Janabaevazizbek

places.title: Galataport and the Karaköy waterfront
places.why: A 1.2 km stretch of the Karaköy and Tophane docks, closed to the public for decades, reopened in 2021 as a waterfront promenade with the cruise terminal hidden underground. It links the old port buildings with Istanbul Modern and the Painting and Sculpture Museum.

photos.file: Galataport from Istanbul Museum of Modern Art in 2024 5623.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

places.title: Istanbul Archaeology Museums and the Tiled Kiosk
places.why: A neoclassical museum built for the royal sarcophagi of Sidon, among them the Alexander Sarcophagus, faces the Tiled Kiosk of 1472, one of the oldest Ottoman buildings in the city, with its tiled portico. Both stand in the outer gardens of Topkapı Palace.

photos.file: Museum of Islamic Art (Tiled Kiosk). Istanbul Archaeology Museums, Turkey.jpg
photos.author: Osama Shukir Muhammed Amin FRCP(Glasg)

places.title: Hagia Irene
places.why: The other great Justinianic church, in the first courtyard of Topkapı Palace, was never turned into a mosque and keeps its atrium and bare brick interior. A large mosaic cross from the Iconoclast period fills the half-dome of its apse.

places.title: Little Hagia Sophia (Küçük Ayasofya Camii)
places.why: The church of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, built by Justinian just before Hagia Sophia, tried out on a small scale a dome over an octagon. Its two-storey colonnade still carries the original Greek inscription on the frieze.

photos.file: Istanbul Little Hagia Sophia exterior in 2006 3295.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

photos.file: Istanbul Little Hagia Sophia interior müezzin mahfili - view from - in 2018 9605.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

places.title: Rüstem Pasha Mosque
places.why: Sinan raised the grand vizier’s mosque on a platform above the shops of the market district, reached by narrow stairs. Its walls, piers and porch are covered with the finest İznik tiles of their age, in tulip, carnation and floral designs.

photos.file: Rüstem Pasha Mosque Interior General view in 2024 0225.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

photos.file: Rüstem Pasha Mosque Interior Main entrance in 2024 0226.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

places.title: Valens Aqueduct (Bozdoğan Kemeri)
places.why: The surviving 921 metres of the Roman aqueduct completed under Emperor Valens still stride across the valley between the third and fourth hills, with Atatürk Boulevard running through its arches. It carried water to the city into the 19th century.

places.title: Zeyrek Mosque (Pantocrator) and Çinili Hamam
places.why: Three Comnenian churches joined side by side formed the monastery of Christ Pantocrator, burial place of Byzantine emperors, on the hill of the old wooden quarter of Zeyrek. Down the street, Sinan’s Çinili Hamam has been restored as a working bath with a museum of its tiles.

photos.file: Molla Zeyrek Mosque exterior NW side in 2006 1347.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

places.title: Şehzade Mosque
places.why: Sinan’s first great imperial mosque, built by Süleyman for his dead son Mehmed, is his first test of a central dome over four half-domes. The garden behind it holds tombs with some of the finest tiled interiors in the city.

places.title: Fatih Mosque
places.architect: Atik Sinan; rebuilt by Mimar Mehmed Tahir
places.why: Mehmed II’s mosque complex, the first imperial foundation of Ottoman Istanbul, stands on the site of the Church of the Holy Apostles on the fourth hill. Rebuilt after the earthquake of 1766, it keeps its large walled precinct of madrasas and tombs.

places.title: Sokollu Mehmed Pasha Mosque (Kadırga)
places.why: A small mosque Sinan built on a slope for the grand vizier, entered up a staircase through the courtyard of its madrasa. The İznik tiles of its mihrab wall and fragments of the Kaaba set in its walls make it one of his most refined works.

places.title: Nuruosmaniye Mosque
places.why: The first imperial mosque in the Ottoman baroque, at a gate of the Grand Bazaar: a single great dome over a cubic hall, a curved courtyard and carved cornices drawn from European models.

photos.file: Istanbul Nuruosmaniye Mosque courtyard entrance side in 2015 1156.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

places.title: Great Palace Mosaic Museum
places.why: Floor mosaics from a peristyle courtyard of the Byzantine Great Palace, with hunting scenes, animals and country life, shown where they were found under a shelter behind the Blue Mosque.

photos.file: Mosaici da un peristilio del gran palazzo di costantinopoli, VI secolo ca., pavimento centro-ovest 02,2.jpg
photos.author: Francesco Bini

photos.file: Mosaici da un peristilio del gran palazzo di costantinopoli, VI secolo ca., pavimento nord-ovest 05 leone alato che azzanna gazzella 1.jpg
photos.author: Francesco Bini

photos.file: Mosaici da un peristilio del gran palazzo di costantinopoli, VI secolo ca., fregio 02 ibis.jpg
photos.author: Francesco Bini

places.title: Kılıç Ali Pasha Complex and Hamam
places.architect: Mimar Sinan; hamam restored by Cafer Bozkurt Architecture
places.why: Sinan’s late mosque for the admiral Kılıç Ali Pasha takes Hagia Sophia as its model on a smaller scale. Its bath, restored by Cafer Bozkurt Architecture after seven years of work, is again a working hamam under its original domes.

photos.file: Istanbul, moschea di Kılıç Ali Pasha, di sinan, 1580-87, esterno 01.jpg
photos.author: Francesco Bini

places.title: Theodosius Cistern (Şerefiye Sarnıcı)
places.why: A fifth-century cistern of 32 marble columns under the old city, restored and entered since 2018 through a light steel-and-glass pavilion that sits between the old houses of the street.

places.title: Beylerbeyi Palace
places.why: The sultans’ summer palace on the Asian shore, in white marble under the Bosphorus Bridge, with two sea pavilions on its quay and terraced gardens behind. Its rooms keep their furniture, Bohemian crystal chandeliers and Hereke carpets.

photos.file: At Istanbul - Wikimedia hackathon boat tour 2025 659.jpg
photos.author: Photograph by Mike Peel ( www.mikepeel.net ).

photos.file: At Istanbul - Wikimedia hackathon boat tour 2025 673.jpg
photos.author: Photograph by Mike Peel ( www.mikepeel.net ).

photos.file: At Istanbul - Wikimedia hackathon boat tour 2025 667.jpg
photos.author: Photograph by Mike Peel ( www.mikepeel.net ).

places.title: Galata Mevlevi Lodge (Galata Mevlevihanesi)
places.why: The first lodge of the Mevlevi dervishes in Istanbul, at the foot of İstiklal Avenue, with an octagonal wooden hall for the whirling ceremony, a garden cemetery of carved tombstones and a fountain.

photos.file: Istanbul Galata Mevlevihanesi Grounds Main Building in 2016 3088.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

photos.file: Galata Mevlevi Lodge - Museum - Cemetery - Istanbul, Turkey (10583382884).jpg
photos.author: David Berkowitz from New York, NY, USA

photos.file: Istanbul Galata Mevlevihanesi Grounds Main Building in 2016 3184.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

places.title: St. Anthony of Padua Church (Sent Antuan)
places.why: The largest Catholic church in Istanbul, in red-brick Venetian neo-Gothic, set back from İstiklal Avenue behind a courtyard and a row of apartment buildings that were built to pay for it.

photos.file: St. Anthony of Padua Church in Istanbul 03.JPG
photos.author: Chris06

places.title: Bulgarian St. Stephen Church
places.why: A church built of prefabricated cast-iron panels, cast in Vienna and shipped down the Danube and across the Black Sea, on the Golden Horn shore at Balat. Its neo-Gothic façades and gilded interior are all metal.

photos.file: Istanbul Stephen of the Bulgars Exterior in 2007 8882.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

places.title: Neve Shalom Synagogue
places.why: The main synagogue of Istanbul, built in 1951 by two young architects of the community in the old Jewish quarter below the Galata Tower, with a large prayer hall lit by a rose window.

places.title: Camondo Stairs
places.why: A double flight of stone stairs that loops down from Galata to the old banking street, Bankalar Caddesi, built by the banker Abraham Salomon Camondo; its interlaced curving flights are one of the best-known corners of Galata.

places.title: Haydarpaşa Station
places.why: The terminus of the Baghdad Railway, a German neo-Renaissance stone castle built on wooden piles at the water’s edge, with its own ferry pier. Its towers mark the Asian shore for anyone arriving by sea.

places.title: Sirkeci Station
places.why: The European terminus of the Orient Express, built by the German architect August Jasmund in an Orientalist style of horseshoe arches, rose windows and striped stone and brick.

photos.author: Bahnhofsfront-Istanbul-Sirkeci.jpg : Martin Dürrschnabel derivative work: Dha ( talk )

places.title: Pera Museum (Bristol Hotel)
places.architect: Achille Manoussos; conversion by Sinan Genim
places.why: The former Bristol Hotel of 1893, rebuilt as an art museum behind its neoclassical façade in 2005. Its collection of Orientalist painting includes Osman Hamdi Bey’s The Tortoise Trainer.

photos.author: The original uploader was Free smyrnan at English Wikipedia .

places.title: SALT Galata (Ottoman Bank)
places.architect: Alexandre Vallaury; conversion by Han Tümertekin
places.why: The headquarters of the Ottoman Bank on Bankalar Caddesi, with a neoclassical façade on one street and an Orientalist one on the other, converted by Han Tümertekin into a public library, archive and research centre.

places.title: Üsküdar: Mihrimah Sultan and Şemsi Pasha mosques
places.why: Two Sinan mosques on the Asian waterfront: Mihrimah Sultan’s, raised on a terrace above the ferry square, and the small Şemsi Pasha Mosque with its madrasa right at the water’s edge. The shore between them faces the Maiden’s Tower and the historic peninsula.

photos.file: Golden Horn - Bosphorous River cruise - Istanbul, Turkey (10582910004).jpg
photos.author: David Berkowitz from New York, NY, USA

photos.file: (Istanbul- Mihrimah-Sultan-Moschee) - LABW - Staatsarchiv Freiburg W 134 Ordner 0299 ohneSig 0008.jpg
photos.author: Willy Pragher

places.title: Kuzguncuk
places.why: A Bosphorus village of wooden houses with bay windows, where a mosque, a synagogue and Greek and Armenian churches stand within a few streets of each other. Its community vegetable garden and the Fethi Paşa woods above make it one of the quietest corners of the shore.

places.title: Küçüksu Pavilion
places.why: A small summer pavilion of the sultans on the Asian shore of the Bosphorus, its richly carved rococo marble façade facing the water.

places.title: Rahmi M. Koç Museum (Lengerhane)
places.why: An industrial museum set in the Lengerhane, the stone and brick Ottoman anchor foundry on the Golden Horn, and in a former shipyard next to it, with ships, trains and machines.

places.title: Feshane (Artİstanbul Feshane)
places.why: The Ottoman state fez factory on the Golden Horn shore, a long hall on a cast-iron frame, restored and reopened in 2023 as a municipal cultural centre.

photos.file: Istanbul Feshane Artİstanbul exterior in october 2023 5160.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

photos.file: Istanbul Feshane Artİstanbul exterior in october 2023 5159.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

photos.file: Istanbul Feshane Artİstanbul exterior in october 2023 5161.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

photos.file: Istanbul Feshane Artİstanbul exterior in october 2023 5162.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

places.title: Müze Gazhane (Hasanpaşa Gasworks)
places.why: The gasworks that lit the Asian side from 1892 to the 1990s: its brick halls, chimneys and gas holders were restored around a public garden as museums and a cultural centre in 2021.

places.title: Cendere Sanat (Hamidiye Pumping Station)
places.why: A pumping station of 1902 that supplied the Hamidiye water network and some hundred fountains of the city, restored by the municipality as an art centre with a glass café pavilion in its garden.

places.title: Bomontiada (Bomonti Brewery)
places.why: The brick halls of the first industrial brewery of the Ottoman Empire, founded by the Swiss Bomonti brothers, converted into a cluster of venues, restaurants and courtyards.

places.title: Florya Atatürk Marine Mansion
places.why: Atatürk’s summer house, a modernist pavilion on piles over the Sea of Marmara reached by a long pier, its white volumes and long windows a manifesto of the young republic’s architecture.

places.title: Istanbul University Faculty of Science and Letters
places.architect: Sedad Hakkı Eldem and Emin Onat
places.why: A long stone-clad building with a colonnaded front, one of the key works of the Second National Architecture movement, which looked for a modern Turkish idiom in classical proportions.

places.title: Hilton Istanbul Bosphorus
places.architect: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill with Sedad Hakkı Eldem
places.why: A slab of honeycomb balconies in a park above the Bosphorus: the hotel that brought the International Style to Turkey and was copied by Turkish hotels for a decade.

places.title: Zeyrek Social Security Complex (SSK)
places.why: Offices broken into small blocks with overhanging upper floors that follow the slope and the scale of the wooden houses of Zeyrek; it won the Aga Khan Award in 1986 as an early example of contextual modern architecture.

places.title: Atatürk Cultural Center (AKM)
places.architect: Murat Tabanlıoğlu (Tabanlıoğlu Architects); original building by Hayati Tabanlıoğlu
places.why: The city’s opera house on Taksim Square, rebuilt by Murat Tabanlıoğlu on the footprint of his father’s 1969 building, behind the same glass façade with its aluminium grid. Inside, a red spherical concert hall hangs in the main foyer.

places.title: İstanbul Modern
places.why: Renzo Piano’s museum on the Karaköy quay replaces an old warehouse with a building raised on slender columns and clad in reflective aluminium tubes, with a roof terrace over the Bosphorus.

photos.file: Istanbul Museum of Modern Art Exterior in 2024 5632.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

places.title: Arter
places.why: A contemporary art museum in a working-class district, clad in three-dimensional diamond-shaped ceramic panels that catch the light, with galleries of different heights and a performance hall stacked inside.

places.title: Beyazıt State Library
places.why: The first public library of the Ottoman Empire, housed in the soup kitchen and caravanserai of the Beyazıt mosque complex, renovated with glass roofs over its courtyards and reading rooms under the old domes.

places.title: Rami Library (Rami Barracks)
places.why: A vast 18th-century Ottoman barracks converted into the largest library in Istanbul with a light-handed intervention that keeps its high single-storey halls and inner courtyards.

places.title: Çamlıca Tower
places.why: A 369-metre telecommunications tower on Küçük Çamlıca hill that replaced the forest of masts on the city’s skyline, its tapering form rising from the landscape to observation decks over both continents.

photos.file: Çamlıca Tower viewed from Galata Tower.jpg
photos.author: Julian Lupyan

photos.file: Çamlıca Tower and Maiden's Tower under construction (52505393321).jpg
photos.author: Joe Wallace from Oamaru, New Zealand

places.title: Istanbul Museum of Painting and Sculpture
places.why: Turkey’s oldest museum of modern art, founded in 1937, moved in 2021 into a converted customs warehouse on the Tophane quay, remodelled by Emre Arolat Architecture with galleries around a tall central void.

photos.file: Istanbul Museum of Painting and Sculpture 1.jpg
photos.author: Antoloji

places.title: Istanbul Naval Museum
places.why: A low building on the Beşiktaş shore whose ground floor is one large hall for the imperial caïques, the long rowing barges of the sultans on the Bosphorus.

photos.file: A view from Istanbul Naval Museum Oct 2013.JPG
photos.author: VikiPicture

photos.file: Istanbul Naval Museum Caique B no date in 2014 03 8339.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

photos.file: Istanbul Naval Museum Caique Bird in 2014 19 8312.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

places.title: Tersane Istanbul (Golden Horn Shipyards)
places.why: Part of the Ottoman imperial dockyards on the Golden Horn, converted into a waterfront district of hotels, shops and cultural spaces around the old stone workshops and slipways.

places.title: santralistanbul
places.architect: Nevzat Sayın (NSMH) and Emre Arolat Architects (conversion)
places.why: The first power station of the Ottoman Empire, on the upper Golden Horn, converted into a university campus and an energy museum that keeps the turbines and the control room in place.

photos.file: Istanbul Bilgi University Santralistanbul Campus in March 2023.jpg
photos.author: Kurmanbek

photos.file: A snowy day in Santralistanbul, March 2022 05.jpg
photos.author: Jelican9

places.title: Zorlu Center and Apple Zorlu
places.architect: Tabanlıoğlu Architects and Emre Arolat Architects; Foster + Partners (Apple store)
places.why: A mixed-use complex at a busy junction with a roof park, a performing arts centre and shops; in its plaza the Apple store by Foster + Partners is a glass lantern over a reflecting pool, with the shop below ground.

photos.file: Zorlu Center - Istanbul, Turkey, Apple Store 06.jpg
photos.author: Mostafameraji

places.title: Apple Bağdat Caddesi
places.why: A pavilion under a floating roof between two travertine walls, set back from the shopping street behind a tree-lined public square.

photos.file: Bağdat Avenue Apple Store in July 2024.jpg
photos.author: Kurmanbek

places.title: Istanbul Sapphire
places.why: At 261 metres one of the tallest towers in the city, with a double glass skin that encloses green terraces, and an observation floor at the top.

photos.file: Istanbul safir 57. katından levent istanbulun en yüksek binasi safir kiler grubun malı istanbul seyir terası by ismail soytekinoğlu - panoramio.jpg
photos.author: ismail soytekınoglu

places.title: Yeşilvadi Mosque
places.why: A contemporary mosque that reworks the classical Ottoman scheme in concrete, with geometric Kufic patterns in gold leaf.

places.title: Beylikdüzü Atatürk Arts and Cultural Center (Beylikdüzü Atatürk Kültür ve Sanat Merkezi)
places.why: A district cultural centre reworked around a 2,000 m² glass-roofed atrium, where a steel staircase planted as a vertical garden doubles as a shortcut and a place to sit without having to buy anything.

places.title: Bruno Taut House
places.why: The house Bruno Taut built for himself on the slope above Ortaköy during his exile in Turkey: a narrow volume on a stone base under a pagoda-like roof that recalls his years in Japan.

places.title: Ataköy (Phases I–II)
places.why: The first large planned housing estate of modern Turkey, built by the Emlak Kredi Bank on the Marmara shore: slab blocks and towers set in green space by the sea.

places.title: Istanbul Textile Traders’ Market (İMÇ)
places.architect: Doğan Tekeli, Sami Sisa and Metin Hepgüler
places.why: Six terraced blocks of shops stepping along Atatürk Boulevard below the Valens Aqueduct, in exposed concrete and brick with reliefs and mosaics by Turkish artists: a modern bazaar answering the old Grand Bazaar.

places.title: Atatürk Library (Atatürk Kitaplığı)
places.why: Sedad Hakkı Eldem’s city library on the slope of Gümüşsuyu, a brutalist building of concrete piers and deep projecting floors that reinterprets the overhanging upper storeys of the Ottoman house.

places.title: Sancaklar Mosque
places.why: A mosque without a dome or a minaret: a long stone wall and a canopy step down a grassy slope to a prayer hall dug into the hillside, lit by slits of daylight along its walls.

places.title: Vakko Fashion Center
places.why: REX finished the abandoned concrete frame of a hotel as the fashion house’s headquarters, wrapping a glass box around a stack of skewed steel volumes, in a few months.

places.title: Yıldız Park
places.why: The wooded hillside garden of Yıldız Palace, the last seat of the sultans, with ponds, glasshouses and the Malta and Çadır pavilions, restored as cafés by the Turkish Touring and Automobile Club.

photos.file: Yıldız palace and park Çadır Kiosk in 2014 8207.jpg
photos.author: Dosseman

places.title: Emirgan Park
places.why: A large wooded park on the hill above the Bosphorus at Emirgan, with three 19th-century pavilions, ponds and lawns; in April it is the centre of the city’s tulip planting.

places.title: Belgrad Forest
places.why: The great forest north of the city that supplied its water: Ottoman dams and reservoirs stand among oaks and beeches, and its trails are the favourite of Istanbul’s walkers and runners.

places.title: Atatürk Arboretum
places.why: Turkey’s first arboretum, founded in 1949 on the edge of the Belgrad Forest: a living collection of trees from around the world planted around ponds and streams.

places.title: Fethi Paşa Grove
places.why: A wooded hillside park above the Asian shore between Üsküdar and Kuzguncuk, with terraces and cafés that look across the Bosphorus to the European side.

photos.author: Original uploaded by Hakantheone (Transfered by Stambouliote )

places.title: Khedive Palace and Çubuklu Grove (Hıdiv Kasrı)
places.why: The Art Nouveau summer palace of the last Khedive of Egypt, with its round tower, on a wooded hilltop above the Bosphorus; its terraces and rose garden are open to the public.

places.title: Mihrabat Grove
places.why: A pine-covered nature park on the hillside above Kanlıca, one of the largest green spaces on the Asian shore of the Bosphorus, with views down to the strait and the Fatih Sultan Mehmet Bridge.

places.title: Nezahat Gökyiğit Botanic Garden
places.why: A botanic garden laid out on land left between motorway interchanges on the Asian side, with themed gardens, ponds and plant collections from across Anatolia.

places.title: Baltalimanı Japanese Garden
places.why: A small Japanese garden in the woods above the Bosphorus, built in 2003 with the help of Istanbul’s sister city Shimonoseki and restored by Japanese gardeners in 2015.

photos.file: Waterfall at Baltalimani Japanese Garden Istanbul 2024.jpg
photos.author: Furkan Akkurt

places.title: Maçka Democracy Park
places.why: A park filling the green valley between Nişantaşı and Dolmabahçe, with lawns and plane trees under the cable car that crosses it to Taşkışla; locals come here to picnic, walk dogs and play.

places.title: Bebek Park (Türkan Sabancı Bebek Parkı)
places.why: A small seaside park in the bay of Bebek, with lawns and old trees on the Bosphorus promenade, where locals come to walk and sit by the water.

places.title: Validebağ Grove
places.why: A large grove on the Asian side that its neighbours saved from construction, with meadows of tall grass, old trees and the 19th-century Adile Sultan Pavilion.

photos.file: Indian peafowl on fallen tree Validebag Grove Istanbul 2024.jpg
photos.author: Furkan Akkurt

places.title: Atatürk City Forest
places.why: A city forest on the hills behind Maslak and Bahçeköy, with marked walking and running trails through oak and pine woods.

places.title: Polonezköy Nature Park
places.why: Woods and meadows around the village founded in the 1840s by Polish exiles, on the Asian side north of the city, with walking trails among chestnut and oak trees.

places.title: Haydarpaşa British Cemetery
places.why: A quiet cemetery of soldiers of the Crimean War and both world wars on the cliff above the Sea of Marmara, next to the Selimiye Barracks where Florence Nightingale nursed the wounded.
